title: User Feedback
levelNote: Beyond one clear constraint up front, the developer repeatedly issued vague fix requests with no symptom or evidence, restated the original spec instead of testing actual behavior, and never checked the AI's unverified runtime claims or the unrequested behavior change it slipped in.

items.title: Scoped the first change with a hard constraint
items.quote: Do not change it, but add to make sure to ignore capitalization of word "The" and "the" since it's a same word.
items.detail: In the opening request the developer front-loaded both the goal (case-insensitive matching of "the") and an explicit constraint ("Do not change it") protecting the rest of the working script from incidental edits. This is real intent ownership: the AI was given a bounded task rather than an open-ended invitation to rewrite.

items.title: Vague bug report offloaded diagnosis to the AI
items.quote: then why is not working? please fix it.
items.detail: After the AI restated the which_fibonacci spec correctly, the developer replied only "then why is not working? please fix it." with no error message, no actual-vs-expected output, and no description of what was tried. This hands the entire diagnostic judgment to the AI (which had to ask for clarification in response) instead of the developer doing the minimal due diligence of running the script and reporting what actually happened. Owning it would have meant pasting the error/output and stating what was wrong, not just asserting brokenness.

items.title: Open-ended "fix this" let the AI unilaterally change behavior
items.quote: then fix this statement "print("Input must be a non-negative integer.")"
items.detail: The request gave no criteria for what "fix" meant. The AI responded by not only rewording the message but introducing an ERROR_MSG constant and changing the except ValueError block from a silent `pass` to printing the error message — a functional behavior change beyond what was asked. The developer never scrutinized or acknowledged this scope expansion; the AI was left to invent both the acceptance criteria and the implementation, and the diff was accepted without comment.

items.title: Verified by re-pasting the spec, not by running the code
items.quote: next_fibonacci takes a non-negative integer and returns the next largest Fibonacci number.  If the argument is itself a Fibonacci number, it should return the next Fibonacci number, not the argument itself.  If 1 is received, next_fibonacci should return 2.
items.detail: This is a verbatim repeat of the requirement already given earlier in the session, sent again after the AI produced a fix, rather than an execution/output the developer actually observed. The same pattern recurs for which_fibonacci. This substitutes restating the spec for testing the code, so the AI's own unverified claim in the prior turn about the script's output ("$ python fibonacci.py 13" -> "7" / "21") was never checked by the developer — no pushback, no independent confirmation, just acceptance and moving to the next ask.
